en_summary: $CRWD has agreed to acquire $ZS in an all-stock deal for $43.9 billion, surpassing Google's $32B acquisition of Wiz as the largest cybersecurity acquisition. Zscaler shareholders will receive 1.135 CrowdStrike shares per share, valuing ZS at approximately $260, a 34% premium to Friday's close. Combined company will have more than $10B in ARR. zh_summary: 韓國媒體報導 Samsung 計劃在中國西安 X2 NAND 晶圓廠增加每月 20,000 片產能線，達滿產。目前 10 萬 V6 + 1 萬 V9；可處理 13 萬。新線專 V9，轉 20-30% V6 至 V9，V9 升至 5-6 萬。設備約 2027 年 2 月，2027 年 11 月完成。
en_summary: Korean media report Samsung plans to add production line for 20,000 wafers/month at X2 NAND fab in Xi’an, China, to full capacity. Currently 100k V6 + 10k V9; can handle 130k. New line to V9, convert 20-30% V6 to V9, raising V9 to 50-60k. Equipment ~Feb 2027, complete by Nov 2027.
text:
Korean media report that Samsung plans to add a production line capable of processing 20,000 wafers per month at its X2 NAND flash fab in Xi’an, China, bringing the fab to its full production capacity.

X2 currently produces 100,000 V6 NAND wafers and 10,000 V9 NAND wafers per month. The fab can handle up to 130,000 wafers per month.

Samsung plans to dedicate the new line entirely to V9 and convert 20–30% of its existing V6 capacity to V9 production. The expansion and conversion would raise X2’s V9 capacity to 50,000–60,000 wafers per month.

Samsung plans to build an electroplating line in unused cleanroom space at X2, with equipment move-in expected around February 2027. The company plans to send engineers from its South Korean operations to Xi’an with the aim of completing the expansion by November 2027.

text:
I think it's good enough to send to all early access users (that have eligible cars) and to anyone who has advanced software updates turned on. Anyone beyond that I would wait.

I find FSD V15 to be a decent bit more timid than V14, which is what we'd expect with a first big version release, which then gets polished out with the dot releases.

The release notes said school zone speed control has improved, but that doesn't seem to be the case in my area based on my testing today. I went through two school zones 5 times to test it. Navigation and some parking behaviors still need work too. I noticed a slight improvement to nag on Hurry and Mad Max modes, but not a huge change. It nags as soon as 35 seconds in some cases on side streets.

One interesting thing that happened today: I was parked in a multi-level parking garage, turned on FSD with my destination already set in navigation, and for some reason it started driving up the parking garage instead of toward the exit lol.

Tesla Reality View, pothole avoidance and pulling into home garages are definitely the stars of the show so far for V15. Those things are great. I really hope we can see specific parking spot selection soon, because that would improve the FSD experience a lot.

Want to understand how the market feels about a company’s debt? 

Look at its yield spread over comparable Treasuries.

That’s the extra yield investors demand to lend to that company.

Examples from http://TreasuryBonds.com for bonds maturing in November 2036:

• Microsoft: +0.60 percentage points
• Meta: +1.46 percentage points

Investors demand more than twice the extra yield to hold Meta’s debt.

Wider spreads generally signal greater perceived credit risk, though liquidity and bond terms also matter.

Search a company and check “Spread vs. Treasury” at http://TreasuryBonds.com.

en_summary: Bears finally got their moment last week after predicting AI top for 4 years, but in 3-6 months this will be seen as just a correction; narrative of $NVDA collapse is extreme as it was at record high Oct 6 nearly $6T, even half guided revenue ~$400B annual, S&P strong earnings, Friday 4.1 SD below 50dma more extreme than 2020/2008, AI buildout accelerating, bears sound smart bulls make money.
text:
The bears are having their moment.

After predicting a top in the AI trade every month for the last 4 years, the bears finally got their moment last week.

However, in 3 to 6 months, we are going to look back at this correction and realize it was just that: a correction.

There is a widespread narrative right now that Nvidia, $NVDA, is quite literally going to collapse. This is a stock that was trading at a record high on October 6th, worth nearly $6 trillion, and the inventor of the most advanced chips in the world (it's not even close).

That's how deeply pessimistic sentiment has become over the last seven weeks.

Even if Nvidia produced half as much revenue as they are guiding for their next fiscal year, this company would still produce close to $400 billion in annual revenue.

Meanwhile, the S&P 500 has posted three consecutive quarters with earnings growth above 25% and eight straight quarters of double-digit growth.

And, sentiment flipped so quickly that the S&P 500 closed the week 4.1 standard deviations below its 50-day moving average on Friday. Not even 2020 and 2008 saw such an occurrence.

The reality is that AI truly is the "next big thing" and the AI buildout is only accelerating.

Bears will sound smart, bulls will make money.
